chunks: From him, from Ṣafwān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, who said:

I asked Abā Ibrāhīm عليه السلام about a man who urinates at night and thinks that urine has touched him, but is not certain. Is it sufficient for him, when he urinates, to pour water over his private part and not dry himself?

He عليه السلام said: “He washes what has become clear to him that it was touched, and he sprinkles water over what he doubts concerning from his body or his clothes, and he dries himself before performing wudu (ablution).”

key_terms.الْبَوْلَ: urine; the source of possible ritual impurity discussed in the ruling
key_terms.ثِيَابِهِ: his clothes; one of the places where doubtful impurity may be considered
key_terms.ذَكَرِهِ: his private part; the place over which water is poured after urination
key_terms.لَا يَسْتَيْقِنُ: he is not certain; indicates the case is based on doubt rather than certainty
key_terms.يَتَوَضَّأَ: he performs wudu (ablution); the purification act mentioned at the end of the ruling
key_terms.يَغْسِلُ: he washes; the required act for what is certainly affected by impurity
key_terms.يَنْضِحُ: he sprinkles; the prescribed act for areas about which there is doubt
key_terms.يُجْزِيهِ: it suffices him; asks whether a certain act fulfills the requirement

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he doubts that urine touched his body or clothes?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling on doubt regarding urine impurity after urination at night. It distinguishes between certainty and doubt: what is certainly affected must be washed, while what is merely doubtful is treated by sprinkling, and one should dry himself before performing wudu (ablution).
